## Claims
- [source-backed] The inspected formal source calls \(\omega\) a “ring involution” and specifies \(s_\lambda\mapsto s_{\lambda'}\); it also states that this sends \(I_{r,n-r}\) to \(I_{n-r,r}\). [source-2, lines 1758-1767]
- [proved] In the integral model \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\), define \(e_m\) by \(H(z)E(-z)=1\), where \(H(z)=\sum_{m\ge0}h_mz^m\), \(E(z)=\sum_{m\ge0}e_mz^m\). The coefficient recurrence shows each \(e_m\in\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_m]\); hence \(h_m\mapsto e_m\) defines an integral ring endomorphism \(\omega\). Applying \(\omega\) to \(H(z)E(-z)=1\) gives \(\omega(e_m)=h_m\), so \(\omega^2=\mathrm{id}_\Lambda\).
- [proved] Jacobi–Trudi and dual Jacobi–Trudi give
  \[
  s_\lambda=\det(h_{\lambda_a-a+b}),\qquad
  s_{\lambda'}=\det(e_{\lambda_a-a+b}).
  \]
  Therefore \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) for every partition \(\lambda\). Thus the source’s displayed assignment is an integral ring involution, not merely a \(\mathbb Z\)-linear basis permutation.
- [proved] For \(r,q\ge0\), with
  \[
  I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda,
  \]
  rectangle transposition gives \(\lambda\subseteq q^r\iff\lambda'\subseteq r^q\); hence \(\omega(I_{r,q})=I_{q,r}\) and induces an integral ring isomorphism
  \[
  \bar\omega_{r,q}:\Lambda/I_{r,q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda/I_{q,r},
  \qquad \bar s_\lambda\mapsto\bar s_{\lambda'}.
  \]
- [proved] For interval ideals
  \[
  J_{r,q;i,j}:=\bigoplus_{\,i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda
  \quad(0\le i\le q,\ 0\le j\le r),
  \]
  one has \(i^j\subseteq\lambda\iff j^i\subseteq\lambda'\). Hence, basiswise,
  \[
  \bar\omega_{r,q}(J_{r,q;i,j})
   =\bigoplus_{\,j^i\subseteq\nu\subseteq r^q}\mathbb Z\bar s_\nu
   =J_{q,r;j,i}.
  \]
  The equivalence also holds when \(i=0\) or \(j=0\), since both rectangles are empty.

## Strategy
Construct \(\omega\) integrally from \(h_m\mapsto e_m\), prove it is involutive, then use the two Jacobi–Trudi determinants to prove its Schur-basis action and the induced quotient/interval equality.

## Gaps
This certificate establishes only the previously missing proof that \(\omega(s_\lambda)=s_{\lambda'}\) and \(\omega^2=1\), including its basiswise interval consequence. It does not establish the parent minimality theorem or the broader requested continuation workflow.
